analyst_view.overall: Early view: Real Sociedad are fifth after four wins in five, but this is the middle of a heavy run (Crystal Palace away in the Europa League on 26 November, Real Madrid on 2 December), and Barrenetxea looks set to miss the rest of 2026 with a hamstring injury, according to one report. Sevilla (sixth) have stalled, 0-0 at home to Alavés after Rubén Vargas missed a penalty, and Peque may be back from his hamstring injury around this date.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, and both teams' season totals support a lively game. But Real Sociedad have scored twice in their last two league games, lose Barrenetxea (who set up the winner against Rayo) and arrive three days after a trip to Crystal Palace, while Sevilla failed to score at home to Alavés. I lean lower, nearer 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners. Real Sociedad's last two games both had 13 corners as Matarazzo's side keep the ball and work it wide, and Sevilla's full-backs pushed on to earn 5 corners against a deep Alavés. I lean higher, around 10-11.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards. Sevilla had four yellows and a red at Getafe and Real Sociedad four bookings at Athletic, so the number looks fair; Aramburu and Yangel Herrera are one yellow from bans, which could make Real Sociedad slightly more careful. I stay close to 5.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots. Real Sociedad's last two games had 28 and 27 shots and Sevilla's 22 and 23, so the number sits right in the middle. Fatigue after Thursday could trim Real Sociedad's pressing, but nothing points clearly either way.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 on target. Real Sociedad managed only 3 on target from 17 shots against Rayo, and Sevilla could not beat Sivera even from the penalty spot against Alavés. Patchy finishing on both sides makes me lean lower, around 7.
